newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower, looking oversold.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower, looking oversold.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply lower, the industrial metal succumbing to further selling despite the big drop Tuesday which some believe was already overdone.
"Copper is certainly undervalued right now unless the market is discounting the seasonal slowdown over the next couple of months," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said.
Most dealers still believed the selloff over the past two sessions and last Friday, was technically based, with no fresh fundamental reason behind the downward spiral.
On COMEX the speculators, who were overwhelmingly long according to the CFTC's latest commitment of traders report to week ended June 7, sold heavily on Tuesday, dealers said.
Open interest in July and for COMEX futures overall, fell more than 4,000 lots Tuesday, but no fresh positions were put on in September, now most-active.

July COMEX copper ended 2.95 cents weaker at 109.20 cents a lb, traded 113.50 to 108.20 cents. September, which has edged ahead with most open interest, settled 1.95 cents lower at 108.80 cents, while spot June went out 3.00 cents off at 109.70 cents.
Volume was heavy at an estimated 17,000 lots an hour before the market closed.
On LME stocks rose 875 Tuesday to 123,125 tonnes, while the cash to three months backwardation was stable Wednesday at $110/$120 after Tuesday's sharp contraction.
Rinehimer said the 12-cent drop in the July contract since last Thursday could well lure the Chinese into the market to buy.
Sales of existing homes in the U.S. rose sharply in May but orders for durable goods weakened.
